description: Media over QUIC relay health: downstream sessions and requests, subscription fan-out, object and byte flow, live edge and FETCH sourcing, and drops and errors.

panels.title: Active sessions
panels.description: Downstream MoQT sessions that finished SETUP and are still open, over native QUIC and WebTransport, for the selected listeners and backends. The series appears with a backend's first successful session, so 0 can also mean no client has connected yet.

panels.title: Session success
panels.description: Share of downstream session attempts whose SETUP exchange completed (result ok). The rest were refused (IP/geo ACL, rate limit, no shared draft, backend ACL, WebTransport Origin), had no matching backend, hit max_sessions, or failed the handshake; the Sessions row breaks them down. Policy refusals are expected on a public relay, so judge this against its usual level; refusals made before routing carry no backend and count under any Backend filter. Reads no attempts while no session is attempted.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(trickster_moq_sessions_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", listener_name=~"$listener", backend_name=~"$backend|", result="ok"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / (sum(rate(trickster_moq_sessions_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", listener_name=~"$listener", backend_name=~"$backend|"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Subscriptions
panels.description: Downstream subscriptions viewers and edge relays hold on the relay right now, across the selected backends. One upstream track can feed many of these; compare with Upstream tracks for the fan-out.

panels.title: Upstream tracks
panels.description: Tracks the relay is sourcing right now: its own live SUBSCRIBEs toward origins plus tracks publishers push to it with PUBLISH. A drop here while downstream subscriptions hold steady means the relay lost its origin or publisher.

targets.expr: sum(trickster_moq_active_subscriptions{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", direction="upstream"} or trickster_moq_publishers_active{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}) or vector(0)

panels.title: Egress
panels.description: Object bytes (payload plus object properties) the relay writes to downstream subscribers and FETCH responses. These are application bytes, not wire bytes: MoQ framing and QUIC/WebTransport overhead are not included.

panels.title: Requests refused
panels.description: Share of downstream control requests (SUBSCRIBE, FETCH, TRACK_STATUS, PUBLISH, namespace requests) the relay refused: unauthorized, unknown track, prefix overlap, publishing not allowed, or an unsupported request type. Requests turned away by the backend's rate limiter never reach the relay and are not in this ratio; see the rate-limit panel in the Requests row. Reads no requests while no request arrives.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(trickster_moq_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", result="refused"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / (sum(rate(trickster_moq_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Delivery drops/s
panels.description: Drop events that cost subscribers objects: oversize incoming objects (the whole incoming subgroup stream is cancelled), objects past a subscriber's delivery timeout (that subscriber's subgroup stream is reset) and full datagram queues. One event can lose many objects. Cache spill drops are excluded here because the group was still forwarded live. Healthy is 0.

panels.title: Relay errors
panels.description: Relay errors over the visible time range: malformed tracks (a publisher or origin sent objects that contradict each other, so the track was torn down and its subscribers ended) and groups that failed to store in the backend's cache. Any malformed track is a publisher or origin bug.

panels.title: Active sessions by listener and backend
panels.description: Open downstream sessions per listener and backend. For native QUIC the listener is the protocol: moq listener; for WebTransport it is the HTTP listener whose HTTP/3 endpoint carried the CONNECT. A session keeps the backend it was routed to for its life, even across a reload that removes that backend. There is no transport label here (the attempts panels split QUIC and WebTransport), and the role label is always downstream: the relay's own sessions toward origins have no session metric.

targets.expr: sum by (listener_name, backend_name) (trickster_moq_active_sessions{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", listener_name=~"$listener", backend_name=~"$backend"})

panels.title: Session attempts by result
panels.description: Downstream session attempts per second at their outcome. ok = SETUP completed; refused = an IP or geo ACL, the session rate limiter, no shared draft, a backend ACL or a disallowed WebTransport Origin; no_route = the SETUP authority and path matched no backend (native QUIC only); busy = max_sessions reached; failed = handshake timeout, bad SETUP or a failed WebTransport upgrade. Refused sessions often carry an empty backend, so they show under every backend filter.

panels.title: Session success ratio by transport
panels.description: Share of session attempts that completed SETUP, per transport: quic is the native moq listener, webtransport is browsers over an HTTP/3 listener. A gap between the two points at transport-specific trouble, such as a WebTransport Origin allow-list or an offered draft list the backend does not accept.

targets.expr: (sum by (transport) (rate(trickster_moq_sessions_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", listener_name=~"$listener", backend_name=~"$backend|", result="ok"}[$__rate_interval])) or sum by (transport) (rate(trickster_moq_sessions_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", listener_name=~"$listener", backend_name=~"$backend|"}[$__rate_interval])) * 0) / (sum by (transport) (rate(trickster_moq_sessions_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", listener_name=~"$listener", backend_name=~"$backend|"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Negotiated drafts (range)
panels.description: Successful sessions over the visible range by the MoQT draft they negotiated (by ALPN on native QUIC, by WT-Available-Protocols on WebTransport). The relay prefers the newest draft both sides speak; old clients lingering on an early draft show up here before a draft is dropped from the accepted list.

targets.expr: sum by (draft) (increase(trickster_moq_sessions_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", listener_name=~"$listener", backend_name=~"$backend|", result="ok"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Requests by type
panels.description: Downstream control requests per second the relay accepted or refused, by type. subscribe and fetch dominate a viewing workload; publish and publish_namespace appear only on backends that accept publishers; other is any request type the relay does not support and is always refused. The dashed red line is the refused part of the total, drawn unstacked.

panels.title: Refusal ratio by type
panels.description: Share of each request type the relay refused. There is no reason label: unauthorized, unknown track, prefix overlap, an unsupported mandatory property and publishing not allowed all count here. A jump on subscribe after a deploy usually means a token or namespace grant changed, or the origin no longer has the track.

targets.expr: (sum by (type) (rate(trickster_moq_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", result="refused"}[$__rate_interval])) or sum by (type) (rate(trickster_moq_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) * 0) / (sum by (type) (rate(trickster_moq_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Rate-limited sessions and requests
panels.description: Over-limit decisions per second from rate limiters attached to moq listeners (unit: sessions) and moq backends (unit: SUBSCRIBE, FETCH and TRACK_STATUS requests), by limiter. limited was refused; counted was over the limit but let through (count mode); full is a new client the limiter's key table had no room for. These series carry no backend label, so the Backend filter does not apply. Empty unless a rate_limiter_name is set on a moq listener or backend.

panels.title: Subscriptions and publisher tracks
panels.description: Live subscriptions across the selected backends: downstream are subscribers attached to the relay, upstream are the relay's own SUBSCRIBEs toward origins (one per track, shared by every subscriber), and publisher tracks are tracks publishers push with PUBLISH (counted per track, not per publisher session). Upstream falling while downstream holds means upstream loss; the relay re-subscribes with backoff while downstream subscriptions stay open.

panels.title: Subscription fan-out by backend
panels.description: Downstream subscriptions per upstream track (upstream subscriptions plus publisher tracks), per backend. This is how many subscribers each track the relay sources is serving on average; higher means the relay is saving the origin more work. Empty while a backend sources no track.

targets.expr: sum by (backend_name) (trickster_moq_active_subscriptions{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", direction="downstream"}) / (sum by (backend_name) (trickster_moq_active_subscriptions{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", direction="upstream"} or trickster_moq_publishers_active{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}) > 0)

panels.title: Objects by direction and delivery
panels.description: Objects per second. in = ingested from upstream subscriptions or publishers on subgroup streams or datagrams; out = written to downstream subscribers on streams or datagrams, or to FETCH responses. Objects the relay pulls from upstream for a FETCH or gap fill are not counted as in (see FETCH objects by source), and oversize objects that were dropped are not counted at all.

targets.expr: sum by (delivery) (rate(trickster_moq_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", direction="in", delivery!="fetch"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Throughput by direction
panels.description: Object bytes per second (payload plus object properties) in from origins and publishers and out to subscribers and FETCH responses. Application bytes only: MoQ framing and QUIC/WebTransport overhead are not counted, so NIC throughput will be higher. Bytes pulled from upstream for FETCH fills are not in the in series.

panels.title: Egress amplification by backend
panels.description: Bytes written to subscribers per byte ingested, per backend: the relay's byte-level fan-out. A value near the subscription fan-out is normal. Because bytes fetched from upstream for FETCH fills are not counted as in, FETCH-heavy workloads overstate this ratio.

targets.expr: sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_moq_bytes_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", direction="out"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_moq_bytes_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", direction="in"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Live edge size by backend
panels.description: Bytes the relay holds in its in-memory live edge (the newest moq.live_edge.groups groups of each track), per backend, on the fullest replica. The dashed line marks the default moq.live_edge.max_size_bytes budget of 64 MiB; the budget is per backend and per process, and is not exported, so adjust the line if you changed it. The value can briefly exceed the budget until the oldest groups are evicted.

panels.title: FETCH objects by source
panels.description: Objects that served FETCH requests and subscription gap fills, by where they came from: live_edge and cache are local (counted as whole groups), upstream was fetched from the origin (counted per object read, before range filtering). These are objects sourced, not objects delivered.

panels.title: FETCH local-hit ratio by backend
panels.description: Share of FETCH and fill objects served from the live edge or the cache rather than the origin. Stuck near 0 usually means groups never spill to the cache (moq.spill off, or cache stores failing; see Errors by class) or the publisher never marks the end of its groups, so past groups are never known in full. Spilled groups also count in the backend cache's own metrics on the Caching dashboard.

targets.expr: (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_moq_fetch_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", source=~"live_edge|cache"}[$__rate_interval])) or sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_moq_fetch_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) * 0) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_moq_fetch_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Drops by reason
panels.description: Drop events per second. oversize = an incoming object above moq.max_object_size_bytes cancelled its whole incoming subgroup stream; delivery_timeout = a subscriber's subgroup stream was reset because an object outlived that subscriber's delivery timeout (a slow viewer); datagram_queue_full = a subscriber's datagram queue overflowed; spill_queue_full = a group was not written to the cache (it was still forwarded live). Stream cancels and resets count once each, however many objects they lose.

panels.title: Errors by class
panels.description: Relay errors per interval, per backend. malformed_track = a track's objects contradicted each other (a duplicate differing in delivery, priority or payload, or an object past the end of its group), so the track was torn down uncached and its subscribers ended with MALFORMED_TRACK; cache = a spilled group failed to store in the backend's cache. Session and request failures are not counted here.

list.name: datasource
list.label: Data source
list.description: The Prometheus-compatible data source that scrapes Trickster's /metrics endpoint.

list.name: job
list.label: Job
list.description: Scrape job(s) holding the Trickster targets.

list.name: listener
list.label: Listener
list.description: moq listeners (native QUIC) and HTTP/3 listeners carrying WebTransport sessions. Applies to the session panels only; listed once a listener has seen a session attempt.

list.name: backend
list.label: Backend
list.description: moq backends (relays). Every moq backend is listed as soon as its relay is built.
